one_star_reviews.text:
I have previously seen Dr Thompson and found him to be very knowledgeable, particularly in relation to orthopaedic and joint issues. He treated a previous meniscus injury of mine and referred me for surgery, and it was because of that experience that I specifically chose to return to him regarding a new knee issue.

Unfortunately, my recent experience trying to actually attend an appointment has been extremely disappointing.

I initially booked a 7:00am appointment and arrived at the practice at the scheduled time, only to be told that the doctor would not be coming in. I rebooked for two days later, but that appointment was then cancelled by the practice the following day.

I decided to try once more and booked another 7:00am appointment. I arrived at the practice this morning as scheduled and was again informed by reception that the doctor was not in.

I declined the offer to reschedule.

I appreciate that unexpected circumstances arise in medical practice and appointments occasionally need to be cancelled. However, having three appointments cancelled in such a short period - including twice arriving at the practice at 7:00am before being told the doctor would not be attending - is not a reasonable level of reliability in my view.

It is particularly frustrating when patients are expected to arrive on time and may face cancellation or no-show fees if they fail to do so. Patients also arrange work and other commitments around medical appointments, and their time deserves similar consideration.

I continue to have a high opinion of Dr Thompson's clinical knowledge, which is why I made repeated attempts to see him. Unfortunately, after this experience I won't be making another appointment.

one_star_reviews.text:
Honestly, one of the biggest nightmares I have ever experienced with a real estate agency. The most embarrassing part is that this company presents itself as a good family business, but our experience was anything but decent.

They sent us a water bill saying we had used 330KL in 11 weeks. That is 330,000L of water. The home had no dishwasher, no pool and nothing that could reasonably explain that usage. We disputed the $480 bill and, miraculously, it was reduced by around $400.

They then tried to charge us $900 to fix a tile they claimed was damaged, when we believed it was simply poorly cleaned by the bond cleaners. I disputed the claim and refused to pay that amount for one tile. Again, the amount being claimed was subsequently reduced to less than half of what they originally asked for.

Tayla Cullen is one of the most rude, picky and unprofessional property managers I have EVER dealt with. I have lived in Melbourne, South Australia and Queensland and have never experienced someone who made renting so difficult.

We lived in the property for only 11 weeks and received 14 entry notices. The owners were constantly arranging things at the property, including quotes to level the yard, replant grass, fill small nail holes, remove bamboo screening that provided privacy to our family and replace a light shade. The same company came back four times with the wrong-sized light shade and eventually it was never fixed.

Once we realised the owners appeared to be planning to move back into the property at the end of our lease, and that we weren't going to get the peace and privacy we expected, we decided to break the lease and move back to Brisbane. We requested that the break-lease costs be waived due to the constant disruption. After the property remained advertised for four weeks and we pointed out that other comparable properties had already leased, we were eventually told the owners were moving back in and the break-lease costs were waived.

Communication was another nightmare. Tayla would sometimes refuse to respond for days and then reply at 4:40pm on a Friday, 20 minutes before the office closed. We found this incredibly frustrating.

There was also an issue with our front door. The entry report showed the door closed and we were later told we had caused damage to the door frame. My sister had photos on her phone showing the damage was already there on the day we moved in. Take photos of EVERYTHING. Open every door, drawer and cupboard.

Inspections were also hours long and resulted in massive lists of nitpicking. One inspection occurred only six weeks after we moved in, when no one was home for most of the time. We were asked to address things such as a weed near the tank, two weeds near the main bedroom window, cars parked on the grass and even two baby chicks outside that weren't ours, which apparently required a pet request.

Long story short, I would absolutely not rent through this agency again. The entire experience was exhausting and unnecessarily stressful.

If you're renting in Queensland, my advice based on our experience:

1. Apply for your bond as soon as you are entitled to. Understand the RTA process and don't simply assume the agent's claims are correct.

2. Contact QSTARS. They provide free tenancy advice to Queensland renters and can help you understand your rights.

3. Take as many photos and videos as possible. Be extremely thorough with your entry report. Document everything.

4. Ask for supporting invoices and evidence for bond claims. Don't just accept a quote or an amount because the agent says you owe it.

5. Check your water bills carefully. Make sure the dates and usage actually relate to your tenancy and ask for supporting documentation if something doesn't look right.

Honestly, just don't rent with these people if you can avoid it. It wasn't worth the stress or money for us. We have had much better experiences elsewhere, and based on our experience, Raine & Horne were far nicer and treated us like human beings.

one_star_reviews.text: Extremely disappointing experience at JB Hi-Fi Moore Park. Our family has been buying phones and electronics from JB Hi-Fi for years, so we are not new customers and we were not asking for anything unreasonable. Unfortunately, our experience with Sammy, or a similar name, the tall blonde lady who appeared to be the Sales Manager, was incredibly unpleasant. The other staff members were actually friendly and genuinely tried to help us, but once she became involved, the whole atmosphere changed. She was rude, dismissive and made us feel as though she did not believe what we were telling her. The phone was not even three months old, so obviously we were not there trying to change a phone for fun. We had a genuine issue and needed help, and being made to feel like we were being dishonest was honestly insulting. When I mentioned my rights under Australian Consumer Law, her response was basically that I could complain to Consumer Affairs if I wanted to. Instead of trying to find a practical solution, she kept suggesting options that were unrealistic for us and did not seem interested in actually resolving the problem. I also found the atmosphere around her very uncomfortable. This is only my personal impression, but the other staff seemed noticeably more reserved when she became involved, and the whole interaction suddenly felt tense and negative. What made it even more frustrating was that we later went to another JB Hi-Fi store in the city and the exact same issue was resolved quickly, professionally and without any drama. The other Moore Park staff were helpful, but the way this was handled by the Sales Manager completely ruined the experience for us. Based on this experience, I would recommend going to another JB Hi-Fi location instead.

My first time getting a pedicure in over 3 years. I chose this place because it was more quiet than the other nail salons in westfields and i didnt want to be rushed. The girl with bleached blonde hair and eyelash extensions was my "nail technician". They gave me a basket of at least 15 different colour pallettes (i didnt count but there was definitely more than i was used to) to choose my shade. I thought that was pretty cool how that they had so much more variety than what i experienced in the past years ago. So i happily spent my time analaysing and trying to figure out what colour I wanted. I also noticed my feet were not in the water for even at least 2 mins before she started cutting my cuticles so it hurt a bit more than i was used to. Halfway through (not long because the pedicures are rushed here), the girl said to her co worker in vietnamese "lựa màu tám tiếng"  which translates to picking colour still 8 hours later.
I am vietnamese so i understood 🤣 it was just so shocking because i have never heard any nail salon talk shit about any clients when i used to get my nails done.
Co worker didnt respond much. Just a polite laugh i assume, which i appreciated (she had a bit of green on the ends of her black hair), she remained focused on her client.
I've never experienced this attitude before when i had my nails done monthly at other salons.
Is it so bad i spend my time while getting the pedicure to choose a colour I am happy with ?
I had 2 colours picked out before the shellac stage, usually the other salons happily test out what I had picked for me to make sure I am satisfied but she just look annoyed, and i had to ask her to test it on my finger nails for me.
Positives were there was free little bottles of water, massage chair, aesthetic environment , $5 off with cash, and all the other staff seemed like they were nice and just keeping to themselves with the occasional casual conversation amongst each other and with clients.
This person ruined my experienced for me , even if the nail job was average i would not have made such an effort to write a review and just move on and go elsewhere but this experience i had not encountered before.
I paid $45 with cash

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with NCH has been nothing short of a nightmare.

It took 13 weeks from slab down to the first brick being laid, and unfortunately the issues continued from there. The initial brickwork was extremely poor, with walls built out of alignment, rooms constructed to incorrect dimensions, and the front of the house requiring three separate attempts before it was built correctly.

Throughout the build, it felt as though many tradespeople showed little pride in their workmanship or respect for the home they were building. We encountered numerous defects, including damaged window frames during glass installation, windows and the front door not being plumb, the front door being cut too short, incorrect tiles being delivered, and the wrong garage door being installed, to name just a few.

What was particularly frustrating was that non-compliant items identified in inspectors’ reports were often ignored by the Site Supervisor and Contracts Manager, and there appeared to be resistance to rectifying the work. On several occasions, when issues were eventually addressed, we were told it was being done as a “gesture of goodwill,” despite the problems arising from defective or non-compliant work.

Many of the issues were attributed to variations or tolerances, and at one point I was even told by the Site Supervisor that measurements did not quite line up because “everyone’s tape measure measures differently.” I was also told that it’s only the English that complain, and that if I hadn’t complained and let the Site Supervisor do his job, things would have got done quicker. If the Site Supervisor had done his job properly, I wouldn’t have had anything to complain about. This was extremely concerning and did little to inspire confidence in the quality control processes on site.

To make matters worse, it took five weeks from PCI to receiving our keys, despite the usual timeframe being quoted as 10–14 days.

In the end, both the Site Supervisor and Client Liaison Manager acknowledged that our build had experienced issue after issue through no fault of our own. However, throughout much of the 12-month build process, we often felt that our concerns were dismissed and that we were made to feel as though our complaints were unreasonable.

I sincerely hope other clients have a better experience, but based on our build, I would strongly encourage anyone considering building with NCH to be prepared for significant challenges and to document everything carefully.

Some customers are also celebrated with slab parties, flowers, champagne and regular engagement throughout their build journey, while others receive none of these things. Some are given thorough onsite meetings where questions are answered and concerns are addressed, while others are rushed through appointments and left feeling like just another number.

What is most concerning is the apparent lack of consistency in customer service. Every customer signs a contract, makes a significant financial commitment and should be treated with the same level of professionalism, communication and respect. The experience a customer receives should not depend on who their supervisor is, how vocal they are, or whether they are willing to promote the company on social media.

I also question why some customers appear to be encouraged to advertise and showcase their build journey while others are not. It creates the impression that certain customers are prioritised because they provide marketing value, while others are left feeling overlooked.

After investing hundreds of thousands of dollars into building a home, customers should not have to compare experiences and wonder why they are receiving a completely different level of service from the same company. one_star_reviews.text:
I’ve been taking my car here for servicing for several years, but after repeated poor service and frustration, I absolutely will not be returning.

The latest experience summed up why.

I was told I’d be better off buying four tyres at once because it would be “cheaper/better” than buying two now and two later. Fair enough — except when I actually asked what the saving was, I was then told there was none: the price per tyre is exactly the same regardless of how many you buy. So why tell me buying four would be cheaper in the first place? Either the staff don’t understand their own pricing or they were simply trying to persuade me to spend more money. Neither inspires confidence.

Then there’s collection. Every single time I book my car in, I make it VERY clear that I need it back by 3:30pm so I can collect my children from school. They make a note of it. And yet, repeatedly, the car is not ready on time.

Even when the work is supposedly finished, collecting it becomes another ordeal because they seem incapable of having the paperwork and payment ready. Somehow another 15–20 minutes gets wasted while they faff around at the counter. When you’re a working parent who has specifically told them you have a hard deadline, this is absolutely infuriating.

This time I asked whether, rather than dealing with the usual collection drama, I could simply come back the following morning to collect and pay. I was told they’re busy between 7:30am and 10:30am, so I should come after that — but even then they couldn’t tell me how long I might have to wait.

I then asked the apparently outrageous question of whether I could BOOK A TIME to collect my own car and pay for the service.

No.

So apparently customers can book their cars in, but expecting this business to organise a convenient time to actually hand the car back and take payment is beyond them.

And then there’s the service logbook.

At my last service, I specifically asked whether they had stamped it. They hadn’t. Worse still, when I checked, I discovered they had ALSO forgotten to stamp it after the previous service.

So after paying them to service my car, I apparently also need to check that they’ve completed the most basic administrative parts of the service myself.

Once might be an oversight. Repeatedly failing to have the car ready when promised, repeatedly wasting my time at collection, being completely inflexible about arranging collection, giving questionable advice about tyre pricing, and forgetting to stamp the service book TWICE is a pattern.

After several years as a customer, I’ve had enough.

If a business can’t manage something as basic as returning a customer’s car at the agreed time and correctly completing the service record, I have very little confidence in the rest of the operation.

I’ll be taking my business elsewhere — and wish I’d done so sooner.

Update: The service manager called me after seeing this review.

I explained that I had booked a taxi to take my kids and me to pick up the car, and how disappointed and inconvenienced I was when the car wasn’t ready for collection at the time I had been promised.

He was very understanding, gave me a discount on the work carried out on my car, and personally drove the car back to my house.

I was very appreciative of the way he handled the situation and the effort he made to put things right.

I’m not removing or changing my original review, as everything I wrote was 100% true and reflects my experience at the time. However, I do think it’s important to acknowledge the excellent follow-up and the steps taken to resolve the situation.

Firstly she asked us to do from 9am-2:00pm, leaving me in a very difficult position of employment and having appointments off the island created an extremely stressful time for us. Upon speaking to other educators, one with over 40,000 members in the group, couldn't believe that we were even asked, and that we agreed. Also they would falsify our son being sick because she couldn't handle it, given I would temperature check him and the cough he apparently had would be miraculously gone when I picked him up and no snotty nose, and once falsy said he had conjunctivitis and after waiting 3 hours at the Cowes Hub, the doctor laughed and said "was it mother Theresa that said that?". Even after our son got KIS funding for an additional educator things only improved a little bit, but we were still asked to drop him off later and pick up earlier based on the AD's rostered day hours, I eventually lost employment because of them and I was continually stressed to the point every time I saw them calling I'd be having panic attacks.

Because of our sons multiple allergies, I started making our son homemade replacement foods that were super healthy using chickpeas. Keep in mind there is no policy stating home made food isn't allowed, or that food isn't allowed to be too delicious that it makes other kids jealous.

Our son came home extremely hungry, scoffing food down and I checked his lunch box to see that he barely ate and one of my Tupperwares is gone, which contained a homemade chickpea mouse. Asking my son what happened and where it was, he said his teacher confiscated it because no unhealthy food is allowed,.I was absolutely shocked because no one called me to verify, confirm or to let me know. I emailed Jas asking and I specifically said "Did child not want it?" she said that due to allergies and it being homemade it goes against policies and it's not fair to have something look like a nice treat because of the other children. No phone call or anything.

Jas failed and refused to show us the policy, but we actually found it and they aren't policies at all, besides no nuts but MY KID IS THE ALLERGY KID.

So not only did Jas impose her own personal beliefs to judge us and shame our child, but she lied about it being a policy.

I of course asked other parents and funnily enough, not only did they confess giving their kids homemade brownies, cookies, cakes ECT and never having their children have food taken away... But their children said "no she doesn't take my food, but she takes Jetts because it's unhealthy". Even other children noticed. Jas also tried to LIE and say she only took it and put it in the fridge because Jett didn't want it.

Remember earlier I said in my first email "did child not want it?" and again she said that wasn't the reason. The only person who has been consistent in their story is my child and other children.

The kindergarten management did not help at all and we had no choice but to move our son immediately to another centre, causing extreme stress, financial strain and a massive mistrust and resulting in me reporting them to the department. Since the move, our Son has improved tremendously, he even says "I love my new kinder, my teacher likes me". Because he even would ask me why Jas was mean all the time.

So if your reading this because you think you might want your children here, either run for the hills or request any class that doesn't have Jas as the teacher.
Im not the only parent who has had issues with Jas and been treated horribly.

⭐ 1-star Google review

Extremely disappointing experience with St.George.

I recently had an issue with a $149 Apple App Store transaction. After Apple refused to refund it, I disputed the transaction with St.George. My initial dispute was rejected, so I escalated the matter through AFCA. St.George subsequently reviewed the complaint and offered the full $149 back, which I accepted.

Unfortunately, the problems didn’t end there. My card and Internet Banking access were blocked, even though I never requested this. When I tried to resolve it over the phone, I couldn’t pass the identification process because I couldn’t provide information such as my CAN and account balance, which I couldn’t access because St.George had blocked my access in the first place.

I then went into a branch and waited approximately 45 minutes because there was only one teller available. When I finally reached the teller, I was told she couldn’t help and that I had to wait for another staff member. Eventually someone was able to restore my access and I successfully logged into the app.

About 10 minutes later, the app had signed me out again and my card was declined when I tried to use it at a shop.

I then called St.George again today to try to get this resolved. I waited approximately 20 minutes on hold, only to finally speak to someone who told me she couldn’t help me and transferred me to another department. I have now been sitting on hold for another 45+ minutes waiting to speak to someone who can actually resolve the problem.

From my experience, St.George appears to be severely understaffed, and it is now seriously affecting the level of customer service. The customer service I’ve experienced throughout this situation has been near zero.

This is an unbelievable amount of time and effort to spend trying to regain access to my own bank account and card.

The $149 was eventually returned, thanks to the AFCA complaint, but the way St.George has handled everything surrounding my card and Internet Banking access has been incredibly frustrating and time-consuming.

I shouldn’t have to spend hours on the phone, wait 45 minutes in a branch, have my access temporarily restored, and then find my card and app blocked again shortly afterwards.

This experience has seriously damaged my confidence in St.George, and I’m now considering moving my banking to another bank.

one_star_reviews.text:
Great doctors and nurses, but very poor reception experience

My wife had a termination at MSI St Kilda in Victoria today. Her experience with the doctor and nurses was very good. They were professional, caring and supportive.

Unfortunately, the reception staff were very rude. There was a miscommunication about her appointment time, and my wife arrived an hour earlier than the time she was given. She had already been fasting for six hours and was in a very stressful situation, but she was asked to leave the clinic immediately and come back at the exact time of her surgery.

We then had to wait outside the clinic for one hour. Her actual surgery started four hours later. The receptionist was disrespectful and spoke loudly, which made my wife feel humiliated at a time when she needed support the most.

If we had another option at the time, we would have walked out and not come back. But my wife needed to have the procedure, so she had no choice but to stay.

I have seen other Google reviews mentioning similar problems with the reception staff, but it does not seem like management is doing anything about it. one_star_reviews.text:
Review: Disappointing Service and Overpriced, Subpar Food at Club Lennox
Rating: 1/5
Date of Visit: Wednesday, 27th August
Time: ~6:10 PM
As regular visitors who spend 10 weeks a year in Lennox Head, we were keen to try Club Lennox after multiple locals recommended it as a great-value spot with good service. Unfortunately, our experience at the bistro on Wednesday evening failed on both counts.
Staggered Food Delivery & Poor Communication
We placed our order for four meals early in the evening at 6:12 PM. The first two meals arrived promptly at 6:20 PM, but the remaining two didn't reach the table until 6:50 PM—a 30-minute delay between guests eating at the same table.
When we initially inquired about the missing meals, the American/Canadian staff member delivering food claimed there were two cooking areas and assured us the rest would arrive in five minutes. When we questioned the delay a second time 30 minutes later, his attitude turned unnecessarily rude, defensively pointing to a sign stating a 30-minute wait time. Given our order was timestamped at 6:12 PM when the bistro was quiet, any expected delays should have been communicated at the register—not 40 minutes after sitting down.
We noticed the exact same issue at the table next to us: an order of four steaks brought out as two early and two late.
Subpar Quality & Questionable Value
The food quality was equally frustrating across all four orders:
* Whiting Fillets (Mains): Heavy on the breading and paper-thin on fish. Despite the menu advertising locally sourced fish, these were clearly frozen, mass-produced crumbed fillets.
* Swordfish (Daily Special): The portion size was roughly the size of a 50-cent coin, making the nearly $50 price tag hard to justify.
* Steak: While visitor/non-member surcharges are expected, charging double the member price (pushing it near $50) for standard club fare is completely out of touch with the quality served.
Between the disjointed kitchen service, rude front-of-house staff, and overpriced, low-quality meals, Club Lennox fell far short of its reputation. We won't be returning, nor will we be recommending it to anyone staying in the area.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience regarding commitment and delays

I am extremely disappointed with my experience with IPG Smart Home regarding my residential building project in Austral.

I entered into the project expecting IPG to honour the commitments and timelines associated with our building arrangement. Considerable time has passed, and despite completing important requirements on my side, construction has still not commenced.

What has been particularly frustrating is the lack of certainty regarding the commencement and completion of the project. After a lengthy period, IPG advised that increased fuel, freight and construction costs meant that proceeding with the originally proposed prefabricated building method would require an estimated 15–20% price increase. Instead, they proposed changing the design and construction approach and involving another building partner.

This is especially disappointing because we had already progressed significantly with the original design and selections. Our signed material selection dated 30 January 2026 identifies the approved model as PINE 25 DUAL KEY + STUDIO with ECOLUX 1 façade.

IPG's latest proposal gives a target of obtaining CDC approval within three months after finalising the revised design and documentation, with completion only anticipated around June–July 2027. After the time already lost, this creates further uncertainty for us.

Building a home is a major financial commitment, and customers reasonably expect clear communication, realistic timelines and commitments to be honoured. The prolonged delay and proposed changes have caused significant frustration, uncertainty and loss of time.

Based on my experience to date, I cannot recommend IPG Smart Home for reliability in meeting building commitments and timelines.

I hope IPG takes responsibility for resolving the outstanding issues, provides a firm and transparent construction programme, and delivers what was agreed without further unnecessary delay.

I will update this review if IPG resolves the matter satisfactorily and completes the project as promised.

Why I wish to volunteer at Atisha Centre?
I don't, but I do.

Buddhism intrigues me but I feel it has many contradictions.

I know that sounds confrontational, even stupid, however I want to understand the contradictions.

I know no other way of cutting through the bull effluent than perhaps volunteering and seeing.

For example, none of us are individuals in the normal sense as believed by common community.  We are all one and we are all the same.  We are the sky and the earth.  Yet Buddhism has a hierarchy that places one above another.

Buddha is both an historical figure and a name for anyone who has attained enlightenment.  Historically there were many Buddha's, but today you can not be a Buddha.

Buddha taught the middle road after growing up in wealth and many years being an ascetic.  However, these days it appears Buddhists wish to attain a cloak of wealth and wear it proudly in the buildings they create and the showy nature of their existence.

These are a small few of the contradictions that Buddhism shows against a teaching that if followed is world class.

I do not want to spend years in an organised religion as I clearly see through most of them.  Hence, volunteering and witnessing your beliefs may be the only way to truly understand.

The reply from management.
From Pauline to Manager Nick Redmond.

Forwarding this email to you as I have difficulty with its content.
Could we talk about this or do you want to answer it as it addressed to both of us.

Warm wishes
Pauline

Nicks reply to me.
Hey

Please try volunteering Bendigo in the link forwarded.

Currently Atisha Centre does not have the capacity to meet your volunteering needs.

Thanks for your interest.
city-logo-stacked-blue.png
Volunteering | City of Greater Bendigo
bendigo.vic.gov.au

Kind regards,

Nick
Centre Director
http://www.atishacentre.org.au

After a discussion with Nick he insinuated that I was being stupid for trying to see things through Buddha's eyes.  He laughed at my comments.

He also became angry with me when I asked simple questions to please help me understand my confusion.

When I pointed out his anger and his disrespect for me asking a simple question, he hung up on me, ending the conversation.

My questions go un answered and my belief that current Buddhism is an organised religious cam have been reinforced and dare I day confirmed.

Such a shame for such a response when a Lay person simply asks for clarification.

AI assist states
Respectful Dialogue in Buddhism
Core Principles

Buddhism emphasizes kindness and understanding in all interactions. Disrespect or attacks against anyone, including lay people, contradict the fundamental teachings of the Buddha. The focus is on fostering constructive dialogue rather than hostility.
Guidelines for Interaction

Constructive Criticism: Lay people have the right to provide constructive feedback about monastic conduct. This is seen as a natural part of growth within the Buddhist community.

Compassionate Response: The Buddha taught that monks should respond with compassion to complaints from lay followers. This includes acknowledging mistakes and apologizing when necessary.

Ethical Conduct

Buddhists are encouraged to adhere to ethical guidelines that promote non-harm and benefit to all beings. This includes:

Avoiding Harm: Do not harm others through speech or actions.
Promoting Understanding: Engage in discussions that enhance understanding and respect for the teachings.

In summary, a Buddhist should not be disrespectful or attack a lay person for asking questions about the Buddha. Instead, they should engage in respectful and constructive dialogue.

This wasn’t something that could simply fall out or become dislodged. It was securely installed and required tools to remove. The wiring had also been cut, and there were holes and damage left in the spray-in tub liner where the equipment had been installed.

We’re talking about thousands of dollars worth of equipment and damage to the vehicle.

What makes the situation even worse is the response from JCS Global. Rather than taking genuine responsibility and properly investigating what happened to property that was clearly present when the vehicle was handed over, they hid behind their terms and conditions and essentially left me to deal with the financial loss myself.

I find it extremely concerning that a vehicle can be transported through a company, arrive without securely installed equipment that was present when it was handed over, have cut wiring and physical damage left behind, and the response is effectively “not our responsibility.”

The whole experience has been incredibly frustrating and has caused unnecessary stress and financial loss.

I would strongly recommend anyone using JCS Global to think twice about what they are trusting them with.

one_star_reviews.text:
2/10/2026 you have still not addressed the issues with the balcony - lights left on 24/7, my privacy, some staff and residents commenting when I am in my backyard. It’s the staff that are loud not the residents.

Camden House: Now that the weather is warming up, the balcony noise issues have started again. Over the last month there were birthday celebrations with children screaming for hours, loud music playing on the balcony, and the balcony blinds left up day and night. The facility is on a large enough block of land for residents to enjoy these events without impacting private neighbouring homes, yet nothing has been done to address this ongoing problem.

There is currently a man on the balcony singing into a microphone and playing amplified music. These issues were first raised with management on 26 April 2024, but the behaviour continues.

Extremely disappointed with the ongoing behaviour from management, some residents with complex behaviours, and some staff at this facility.

As a neighbour, I have experienced repeated issues with staff, residents, and even visitors making comments about me and watching me from the Camden House balcony while I am in my own backyard. Comments such as a male staff member saying “is that her laundry” and then another male staff member saying “you should be alright”, “Is she in the backyard?”, “She is in the backyard”, “Go away” and a female staff member telling a resident to “ignore her”, “she is planting another tree”, “what is she doing” while I was gardening or “she is going to make noise now” if they see me with the lawnmower are completely inappropriate and make me feel uncomfortable in my own home.

Both Estia Health Camden and Estia Health head office have been made aware of this, yet the matter remains unresolved.

Living next to this facility feels like living beside a venue that operates seven days a week, 365 days a year. Noise includes daily activity, morning teas/afternoon teas and lunches on the balcony, residents and staff spending long periods of time on the balcony, staff team meetings (which I can hear word for word), music, balcony doors left open so singing and piano sessions carry across, maintenance noise, strong cooking smells, and balcony lights left on all night. The balcony is also used for birthday parties which go for 3 hours, celebrations of life which can go all day, and for visitors.

It is also unclear why the noisiest and most active part of the building was constructed directly on the private residential fence line instead of facing inward toward their own property. Respectful neighbours deserve respectful treatment in return, and unfortunately that has not been my experience.

For comparison, the Homes NSW residents on the same block back onto private properties and you wouldn’t even know they were there.

I hope Estia Health takes these concerns seriously and finally addresses the ongoing impact their operations are having on private neighbouring homes.

one_star_reviews.text: Thankfully I don't need to use 13Cabs often.  The level of service has deteriorated dramatically since we first used them 5 years ago.  Started calling for a cab at 10.15am to connect with a train leaving Echuca Station at 11.17am.   Call connected to an automated service which is atrocious.  I speak very clearly and had to repeat my address 4 times before I was connected to an operator.  The automated service was trying to have me picked up at just about every local church ... go figure! The customer service operator had no personality but at least I was able to book a cab.  Waited over half an hour until cab arrived, I received a message that the driver, John, had arrived at my address, however it was another 10 minutes until the cab arrived.  Driver just automatically opened the boot to let me put my own luggage in there without any attempt assisting.  Cab  looked run down with damaged seats and needed a clean, I felt grotty upon arriving at destination.  Hopefully will not have to use their service in the future.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was extremely disappointed with my experience with Dr David Knight at Demeter Fertility.

I went to a fertility specialist because I wanted clear, specialist advice about my fertility and, most importantly, my realistic prospects of having a child using my own eggs. Despite lengthy consultations and an extraordinary amount of blood testing, I left without clearly understanding the answers to those fundamental questions.

A significant amount of consultation time was spent discussing topics I did not expect to form such a substantial part of a fertility consultation, including mindfulness, CBT, books and podcasts, neuroplasticity, psychedelics, ketamine (the discussion of psychedelic substances particularly shocked me, as I am highly conservative about the use of even medically prescribed medications, which I made clear to Dr Knight) and broader health and lifestyle optimisation. This was not what I had gone to a fertility specialist to discuss.

The discussion even included Margaret Thatcher, how dementia affected her, whether she would have been aware of what was happening to her, and this being linked to mental health, awareness and thoughts. I had absolutely no interest in discussing Margaret Thatcher or dementia during a fertility consultation and could not understand what this had to do with why I was there.

I appreciate that general health can be relevant to fertility and pregnancy. However, I do not believe this justified the extent to which other areas of my health dominated the consultation. I have separate specialists for my mental health, chronic pain and weight management. I do not understand why a fertility specialist would spend so much consultation time concentrating on areas outside his specialty when I was seeking fertility advice. If Dr Knight considered health optimisation important, he could have simply identified the relevant issues and recommended I address them with my appropriate treating practitioners.

The blood testing was particularly upsetting. I was sent for a very large number of blood tests and became so bruised from the blood draws that I had bruising over my arms. During the first collection, after only part of the requested bloods had been taken, I fainted. I had to return on two further days to complete the tests. After going through all of that, I was extremely frustrated to learn how much of the extensive testing related to broader general health and health optimisation rather than directly answering my fertility questions.

What made the experience worse was that I still left without a clear understanding of what my results meant for my realistic chances of having a baby using my own eggs. It was only after I complained in writing that Dr Knight provided a much clearer explanation of the fertility prognosis I believe should have been explained during the consultation itself.

I was also unhappy with the billing and refund process. I requested a refund because I did not believe I had received the fertility service I had attended and paid for. I sought a full refund because, in my view, given the service I received, Dr Knight did not deserve to retain one cent of the fee I paid.

My experience with staff member Janine Marsden regarding the refund was also extremely disappointing. I found her extremely rude when I told her I expected every cent refunded because, in my view, Dr Knight did not deserve to retain any of it. Regardless of whether she agreed with my complaint, I did not appreciate the manner in which I was spoken to when raising concerns about a service I had paid for.

I appreciate that other patients may have a different experience, but based on mine, I would not return.

⭐ 1/5 — Unacceptable return policy.
My complaint is specifically about Devil’s Paradise’s return policy.
I purchased an intimacy product and came back just TWO DAYS later with the receipt. The product had NEVER been opened or used and was still completely SEALED in its original packaging. Despite this, they refused to accept the return.
I completely understand refusing returns of intimacy products that have been opened, unsealed or used for hygiene reasons. But that was absolutely NOT the case here. The product had NEVER been opened or used.
What I find unacceptable is that a customer can return almost immediately, with proof of purchase and a completely sealed and untouched product, and still be told there is no return option.
Customers should be made VERY CLEARLY aware of this policy before purchasing. Had I understood this before paying, I would never have made the purchase.
After this experience, I would NEVER recommend Devil’s Paradise to anyone. I certainly will never shop there again. Extremely disappointing customer service and an unacceptable return policy.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had my vehicle serviced here and was extremely disappointed with how the situation was handled afterwards.

I was told I needed the rear differential oil changed and was quoted $400 for the job. I decided to have it done elsewhere and was charged $150 for the same service.

When I returned with proof that the differential oil had been completed elsewhere, I asked them to sign my warranty/service book. I was then told, quite bluntly, “No, we’re not signing it.” They literally stood there and refused to sign the book even though they did the service.

I understand that businesses can have their own policies, but refusing to sign my warranty book simply because I chose to have a particular service completed elsewhere especially when I had already paid for the service was extremely disappointing and unprofessional.

Also when the service was completed, they stated that 5+ extras needed to be done yet had these looked at at another mechanic and it’s all false.

I won’t be returning, and based on this experience, I would encourage others to get a second quote before doing additional work.
